extracted.intended_audience: legislators, statesmen, and students of political theory (readers of classical political essays)
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and substantive criteria for composing or evaluating a political-constitutional critique: attention to institutional design (legislature, executive, judicature, army), safeguards, and practical consequences of reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for local attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: No man ever was attached by a sense of pride, partiality, or real affection, to a description of square measurement. We begin our public affections in our families... These are inns and resting-places. Such divisions of our country as have been formed by habit, and not by a sudden jerk of authority, were so many little images of the great country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutions and policies should respect historical, provincial, and habitual local attachments rather than attempt to fuse citizens by abstract/geometrical divisions. Artificially imposed, purely administrative identities risk destroying the natural affections that bind people to the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative checks and fundamental laws
rubrics_metrics.description: We see a body in its constitution with every possible power and no possible external control. We see a body without fundamental laws, without established maxims, without respected rules of proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legislature must operate within fundamental laws, established maxims and respected procedures; absolute or unchecked assemblies produce instability and arbitrary rule. Evaluate whether a legislative body has meaningful external controls and procedural constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a senate or council
rubrics_metrics.description: They have forgot to constitute a senate, or something of that nature and character... something to which foreign states might connect themselves, -- something which might give a bias and steadiness, and preserve something like consistency in the proceedings of state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republican systems require an intermediate, deliberative council (senate/council) to provide steadiness, continuity, and an institutional counterweight to a single active assembly. Absence of such a body is a structural defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive with deliberative discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Their first executive officer is to be a machine, without any sort of deliberative discretion in any one act of his function. At best, he is but a channel to convey to the National Assembly such matter as may import that body to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The executive should possess genuine deliberative discretion and not be a mere ceremonial channel. An executive deprived of discretion cannot direct measures or provide effective administration; consider whether the executive role includes meaningful authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive as fountain of justice and dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: The king of France is not the fountain of justice. The judges... are of his nomination. He neither proposes the candidates nor has a negative on the choice. He is not even the public prosecutor... It is impossible to place anything called royalty in a more degrading point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocating judicial and prosecutorial prerogatives affects the dignity and efficacy of the executive. Stripping the executive of traditional judicial roles can degrade both the office and the administration of justice; evaluate how juridical powers are distributed and their symbolic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive must have means to reward service
rubrics_metrics.description: What sort of person is a king to command executory service, who has no means whatsoever to reward it:--not in a permanent office; not in a grant of land; no, not in a pension of fifty pounds a year; not in the vainest and most trivial title?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To secure loyal and effective execution of policy, the executive (or those who lead execution) must have legitimate means to reward service (offices, pensions, honors). Without such means, officials will be motivated only by fear or expediency, undermining zeal and stable governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers chosen by affairs not affections
rubrics_metrics.description: Those ministers... were chosen by affairs, not by affections... acted in the name of and in trust for kings, and not as their avowed constitutional and ostensible masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers should be selected for competence and suitability to affairs rather than personal affection or factional imposition. Selection by circumstance rather than by patronage preserves public trust and effective administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers need confidence and discretion (not hollow responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to execute, without power; they are to be responsible, without discretion; they are to deliberate, without choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting ministers responsibility without corresponding discretion and power renders responsibility meaningless and governance ineffective. Assess whether officeholders have both authority and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of peace and war with proper checks
rubrics_metrics.description: It was in your power to leave to your king the right of peace and war... There is no other way of keeping the several potentates of Europe from intriguing distinctly and personally with the members of your Assembly...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The constitution of war/peace powers must be handled carefully: vesting them in the executive can prevent foreign intrigue but is hazardous unless accompanied by auxiliary trusts and checks. Evaluate how foreign-affairs prerogatives are assigned and what controls exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent, permanent judicature
rubrics_metrics.description: They composed permanent bodies politic, constituted to resist arbitrary innovation; and from that corporate constitution, and from most of their forms, they were well calculated to afford both certainty and stability to the laws. They held for life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judiciary with permanence (life tenure or equivalent security) and corporate continuity functions as a bulwark against arbitrary power and preserves legal stability. Temporary or insecure judicial appointments weaken the rule of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid elective, temporary, local judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Elective, temporary, local judges, such as you have contrived, exercising their dependent functions in a narrow society, must be the worst of all tribunals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term, locally-elected judges are highly susceptible to faction, partiality, and local pressures; they do not protect minorities or strangers and undermine impartial justice. Favor institutional designs that minimize such vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial independence from legislative instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to be sworn to obey all the rules, orders, and instructions which from time to time they are to receive from the National Assembly... Any studies which they have made (if any they have made) are to be useless to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges must not be bound to follow ad hoc legislative instructions that can alter the rule of decision mid-cause. Subordination of judges to legislative orders destroys the ground of law and makes the judiciary an instrument of the governing power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of remonstrance from execution
rubrics_metrics.description: It would have been prudent... to preserve their ancient power of registering, and of remonstrating... Your vesting the power of remonstrance... in your principal executive officer, whom... you persevere in calling king, is the height of absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The power to register or remonstrate against legislation should be lodged in a body external to the executive who would execute the laws. Vesting remonstrance in the executing officer conflates counsel and execution and removes a key check on legislative excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative bodies must be subject to law
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative bodies are carefully exempted from the jurisdiction of these new tribunals... Those who execute public pecuniary trusts ought of all men to be the most strictly held to their duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and executive corporations handling public funds and duties must be subject to legal jurisdiction and coercion; exempting them creates impunity and enables oligarchic or factional capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: High court independence from legislative inquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: If great care is not taken to form it in a spirit very different from that which has guided them in their proceedings relative to state offences, this tribunal, subservient to their inquisition, 'the Committee of Research,' will extinguish the last sparks of liberty in France.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supreme criminal or state judicature must be formed independently of legislative inquisitions or committees that investigate members; avoid allowing the legislature to evoke or direct the high court at will, and locate such courts to reduce local partisan pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army as instrument of civil government; avoid military democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of things requires that the army should never act but as an instrument. The moment that, erecting itself into a deliberate body, it shall act according to its own resolutions, the government... will immediately degenerate into a military democracy: a species of political monster which has always ended by devouring those who have produced it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military forces must remain under clear civil control and disciplined obedience; the emergence of independent military deliberative bodies leads to dictatorship or military democracy. Institutional design must secure subordination of the armed forces to lawful civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective disciplinary measures for military disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: After the secretary at war had stated that the regiments had paid no regard to oaths... they propose--what? More oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses to military insubordination require decisive legal and disciplinary measures (courts-martial, breaking or decimating corps, inquiries into murders of commanders), not merely proclamations or additional oaths. Evaluate whether remedies are substantive and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and consistency of laws over occasional decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: The vice of the ancient democracies, and one cause of their ruin, was, that they ruled, as you do, by occasional decrees, psephismata. This practice soon broke in upon the tenor and consistency of the laws; it abated the respect of the people towards them, and totally destroyed them in the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal systems should favor consistent, general laws rather than ad hoc occasional decrees. Frequent, situational decrees erode the coherence and authority of the law; draftsmen should aim for clarity, generality, and permanence.
